findings.claim: The rear-seam Hebrew splice at MT 6:1 is glossed with a WEB run that extends well past the splice.
findings.grounds: The splice is "בִּשְׁנַת מוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ עֻזִּיָּ֔הוּ וָאֶרְאֶ֧ה" (oshb:Isa.6.1, byte tier - re-collated byte tier), which ends at the vision verb; the paired gloss runs to “In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up;” (web:Isa.6.1), i.e. it also renders "אֶת אֲדֹנָ֛י יֹשֵׁ֥ב עַל כִּסֵּ֖א רָ֣ם וְנִשָּׂ֑א" (oshb:Isa.6.1, byte tier), which stands outside the splice. Gloss extent exceeds splice extent.
findings.proposed_change: Re-cut the gloss to the WEB extent that matches the splice - the verbatim WEB prefix “In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw” (web:Isa.6.1) - or extend the splice through "{601_throne}". No span change.

findings.claim: The row's nominated rear-seam warrant - that MT 7:18 opens an oracle cycle which "names no speaker and addresses no one directly" - does not survive the bytes of the cycle it characterises, and it is the warrant the row expressly prefers over the day-formula.
findings.grounds: The row demotes the only formal signal at the seam ("The seam is best argued not from the day-formula's own recurrence, which recurs across web:Isa.7.18-Isa.7.25 and which cannot discriminate the cut on its own, but from a frame-mode shift at MT 7:18 itself") and rests the seam on the frame-mode characterisation instead, so that characterisation is load-bearing. MT 7:25, inside the characterised cycle, carries "לֹֽא תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה" (oshb:Isa.7.25, byte tier), which the row's own second witness renders as a direct second-person address, “All the hills that were cultivated with the hoe, you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns;” (web:Isa.7.25) - a verse inside the range this row lists at web:Isa.7.18-Isa.7.25. The identical warrant sentence is carried at the facing row for web:Isa.7.18-Isa.7.25, where it stands two sentences from that row's own contrary statement that the cycle is "addressed to the same audience as the preceding narrative" and from its rejected-alternative ground that "the four share one addressee". Honest limit: no morphology layer is available in the staged extract, so the person of "לֹֽא תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה" (oshb:Isa.7.25, byte tier) cannot be machine-settled from the pointed bytes alone (2ms and 3fs are both open); that ambiguity is itself a reason the characterisation cannot carry a seam, and the in-field contradiction stands regardless of how the form is parsed.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: delete the "names no speaker and addresses no one directly" clause and re-argue the rear seam from byte facts actually at the seam - the close of the named-participant narrative scene at MT 7:17 and the verse-initial oracle-frame onset "{718_ext}" (oshb:Isa.7.18, byte tier) - with the tier-3 petuchah at oshb:Isa.7.17 kept as disclosed corroboration only. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: "Four verse-initial speech onsets punctuate the span" is a digit whose swept object is unnamed and which is short for the object as stated.
findings.grounds: MT 7:12, inside the span, opens verse-initially on "וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָחָ֑ז" (oshb:Isa.7.12, byte tier) - a fifth verse-initial speech onset, unnamed by the row; MT 7:2 likewise opens on the report formula "וַיֻּגַּ֗ד לְבֵ֤ית דָּוִד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר" (oshb:Isa.7.2, byte tier). The four the row does name (oshb:Isa.7.3, oshb:Isa.7.7, oshb:Isa.7.10, oshb:Isa.7.13) are the divine/prophetic frame onsets, but the row counts the unqualified class "verse-initial speech onsets", and the campaign's frame-owner count discipline requires the object be named before the digit. The digit is not alone load-bearing: MT 7:12's reply sits inside the same third-person frame and does not reopen the row.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: name the object (e.g. "four verse-initial divine-frame speech onsets") or restate the digit to include MT 7:12. No span change.

findings.claim: The rejected alternative is set aside on the ground that "no tier-1 frame or addressee shift separates the sign speech from the surrounding narrative scene", but the row's own splices place a ruled tier-1 vocative-imperative onset immediately before the sign speech.
findings.grounds: The row itself splices "וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְעוּ נָ֖א בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד" (oshb:Isa.7.13, byte tier) - a verse-initial speech formula plus imperative plus vocative - and the addressee shifts across it from the 2ms address to Ahaz, "שְׁאַל לְךָ֣ א֔וֹת" (oshb:Isa.7.11, byte tier), to the 2mp of the house of David, "הַמְעַ֤ט מִכֶּם֙" (oshb:Isa.7.13, byte tier). Vocative and imperative onsets explicit in the bytes are ruled tier-1 in this book's frame spine, so the blanket ground as written is contradicted by the row's own cited evidence. The span itself is defensible under the frame-plus-speech default-larger-unit rule; only the stated ground fails.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: restrict the ground to the exact cut the rival proposes (web:Isa.7.13|web:Isa.7.14 and web:Isa.7.16|web:Isa.7.17), or re-argue the dismissal from the frame-plus-speech default-larger-unit rule. No span change.

findings.claim: Two splice/gloss extent mismatches in the row's own fields.
findings.grounds: At MT 7:13 the splice "וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְעוּ נָ֖א בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד" (oshb:Isa.7.13, byte tier) opens with the speech verb, but the paired gloss “Listen now, house of David” (web:Isa.7.13) drops WEB's rendering of that verb (“He said,”). At MT 7:3 the splice "וּשְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב" (oshb:Isa.7.3, byte tier) is glossed “Shearjashub your son” (web:Isa.7.3), which also renders "בְּנֶ֑ךָ" (oshb:Isa.7.3, byte tier), a token outside the splice.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: re-cut each gloss to its splice extent, per the quote/gloss parity repair rule. No span change.

findings.claim: A recurrence digit ships without its tier named, and the digit holds only at consonantal-skeleton tier.
findings.grounds: The row writes "the first of the book's three עמנו אל sites (sweep: 3 verses)" with no tier label. Re-swept as verse counts: the unpointed consonantal run gives 3 verses (MT 7:14, MT 8:8, MT 8:10) at skeleton tier, while the pointed form "עִמָּ֥נוּ אֵֽל" (oshb:Isa.7.14, byte tier) is byte-identical at only 2 verses (MT 7:14, MT 8:8). The tier-disclosure standard requires every recurrence claim to be tier-labelled at write time.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: label the digit "(sweep: 3 verses, consonantal-skeleton tier)" and, if the pointed form is meant, carry the byte-tier digit of 2. No span change.

findings.claim: The row's nominated front-seam warrant - an "impersonal formulaic oracle cycle that names no speaker and addresses no one directly" - is contradicted twice inside the row's own boundary_rationale and by the bytes of the row's own closing verse.
findings.grounds: The same field states the seam "is best argued not from the day-formula's own recurrence ... but from a frame-mode shift at MT 7:18 itself", making the characterisation load-bearing; two sentences later the same field calls the unit "one oracle cycle addressed to the same audience as the preceding narrative", and the rejected alternative adds that "the four share one addressee ... lacking any addressee shift". The row's own closing verbatim WEB quotation carries the direct address it denies: “All the hills that were cultivated with the hoe, you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns; but it shall be for the sending out of oxen, and for sheep to tread on.” (web:Isa.7.25), against MT bytes "לֹֽא תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה" (oshb:Isa.7.25, byte tier). Honest limit: with no morphology layer staged, the person of "לֹֽא תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה" (oshb:Isa.7.25, byte tier) is not machine-settleable from the pointed bytes (2ms and 3fs both open) - which is itself a reason the characterisation cannot carry a seam; the in-field self-contradiction stands independently of the parse.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: delete the "addresses no one directly" clause; re-argue the front seam from the verse-initial oracle-frame onset "{718_ext}" (oshb:Isa.7.18, byte tier) taken together with the close of the named-participant narrative scene at MT 7:17, and reconsider confidence (currently medium with frontier_flag_considered false) once the warrant is restated. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: The "45 verses book-wide at the bare “in that day” form" digit carries no tier label and is wrong under the only tier named in its own parenthetical.
findings.grounds: The parenthetical reads "(sweep: 13 verses book-wide at the extended, accent-stripped form; 45 verses book-wide at the bare “in that day” form)". Re-swept as verse counts from the staged text: the extended opener "וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא" (oshb:Isa.7.18, byte tier) gives 13 verses at accent-stripped tier - the row's first digit re-verifies exactly. The bare form "בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא" (oshb:Isa.7.18, byte tier) gives 41 verses at accent-stripped tier (that tier retains meteg, which separates MT 2:11, 2:17, 3:7, 29:18), 45 verses at consonantal-skeleton tier, and 12 verses at byte tier. The shipped 45 is therefore a skeleton-tier count presented with no tier of its own inside a parenthetical whose only named tier is accent-stripped, where the correct digit is 41. Not alone load-bearing: the row expressly declines to argue the seam from this recurrence.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: label the digit's tier - "45 verses book-wide at the bare form, consonantal-skeleton tier" - or restate as "41 verses ... accent-stripped". No span change.

findings.claim: device_notes narrates the staging pipeline's tooling composition rather than a fact about the witnesses.
findings.grounds: The field reads "no morphology layer is staged to settle it" - workflow/administrative register about what the extract carries, not a claim about MT or WEB. The evidentiary point it makes is legitimate and byte-anchorable (the held name-vs-address construal of "כִּ֥י עִמָּ֖נוּ אֵֽל" (oshb:Isa.8.10, byte tier) against oshb:Isa.8.8 and oshb:Isa.7.14 turns on a form class the pointed bytes leave open); only the pipeline-referential phrasing is out of register. All other checks on this row pass: both splices re-collate at byte tier at their cited refs, both curly-quoted WEB runs are verbatim, and the span-relevant parashah symmetry set (SAMEKH at MT 8:4 front seam, SAMEKH at MT 8:8 close) is fully disclosed at the correct types with single-witness labels.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: recast as a claim about the witnesses (e.g. that the pointed bytes leave the form class open and both witnesses' renderings are compatible with either construal). No span change.

findings.claim: The closing splice is the whole of MT 8:10 but its paired gloss renders only the verse's final clause.
findings.grounds: The splice is "עֻ֥צוּ עֵצָ֖ה וְתֻפָ֑ר דַּבְּר֤וּ דָבָר֙ וְלֹ֣א יָק֔וּם כִּ֥י עִמָּ֖נוּ אֵֽל" (oshb:Isa.8.10, byte tier - the whole verse), and the paired gloss is “for God is with us” (web:Isa.8.10), which renders only "כִּ֥י עִמָּ֖נוּ אֵֽל" (oshb:Isa.8.10, byte tier). Gloss extent falls far short of splice extent.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: either cut the splice to "{810_ki}" or extend the gloss to the verbatim whole-verse WEB run “Take counsel together, and it will be brought to nothing; speak the word, and it will not stand, for God is with us.” (web:Isa.8.10). No span change.

findings.claim: A recurrence digit ships without its tier named, and the digit holds only at consonantal-skeleton tier.
findings.grounds: device_notes writes "the third and last of the book's three Immanu-El sites (sweep: 3 verses)" with no tier label. Re-swept as verse counts: 3 verses (MT 7:14, MT 8:8, MT 8:10) at consonantal-skeleton tier; the pointed form "עִמָּ֥נוּ אֵֽל" (oshb:Isa.7.14, byte tier) is byte-identical at only 2 verses (MT 7:14, MT 8:8), MT 8:10's own pointing differing inside the run. The tier-disclosure standard requires the tier named at write time on every recurrence claim.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: label the digit "(sweep: 3 verses, consonantal-skeleton tier)". No span change.

findings.claim: The front seam at MT 8:22|MT 8:23 (= web:Isa.8.22|web:Isa.9.1) rests on a thematic tonal turn after the row itself disqualifies the only formal marker standing at MT 8:23.
findings.grounds: The row argues "the seam rests on the turn from darkened lands to light and glory the verse carries, not on the particle", having shown that the verse-initial "כִּ֣י" (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1, byte tier) recurs verse-initially at oshb:Isa.9.3 (= web:Isa.9.4), oshb:Isa.9.4 (= web:Isa.9.5) and oshb:Isa.9.5 (= web:Isa.9.6). No ruled tier-1 signal - frame onset, speech formula, vocative, imperative onset or addressee shift - is named at oshb:Isa.8.23 (= web:Isa.9.1), and the tier-3 parashah layer records no mark at MT 8:22, so the front seam as written carries no byte-standing seam signal at all. A byte-anchored candidate the row leaves unused stands in that verse's own bytes: the temporal-contrast pair "כָּעֵ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן" ... "וְהָאַחֲר֖וֹן הִכְבִּ֑יד" (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1, byte tier).
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: re-argue the front seam from the temporal-contrast frame in oshb:Isa.8.23's (= web:Isa.9.1's) own bytes, or drop confidence from medium to medium_low given that the span carries MT 9:5-6 (= web:Isa.9.6-9.7), a registered expected-low-confidence region. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: The rationale's closing rear-seam warrant contradicts the concession the same field makes about the same span.
findings.grounds: The field concedes "the unit is read as one sustained declaration, not because no fresh subject or addressee arises - both do", naming "הָעָם֙ הַהֹלְכִ֣ים בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ" (oshb:Isa.9.1 = web:Isa.9.2, byte tier) as the fresh nominal subject and "הִרְבִּ֣יתָ הַגּ֔וֹי" (oshb:Isa.9.2 = web:Isa.9.3, byte tier) as the turn to second person. It then closes "No addressee or subject marker reopens before web:Isa.9.8's fresh declarative sentence, so the throne clause stays inside this unit." As written the two cannot both stand. The rear seam does not fall with it - the fresh declarative subject "דָּבָ֛ר שָׁלַ֥ח אֲדֹנָ֖י" (oshb:Isa.9.7 = web:Isa.9.8, byte tier) and the tier-3 SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.9.6 (= web:Isa.9.7) both hold - so this is a defective warrant rather than a boundary defect.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: scope the closing sentence explicitly (e.g. no further subject or addressee marker reopens after the birth clause at oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6) or delete it and rest the rear seam on the fresh declarative subject at oshb:Isa.9.7 (= web:Isa.9.8). No span change.

findings.claim: The closing splice and its paired gloss render different clauses of the same verse, and two further splice/gloss extents in the field do not match.
findings.grounds: The closing splice is the doubled ketiv/qere token pair "לםרבה לְמַרְבֵּ֨ה" (oshb:Isa.9.6 = web:Isa.9.7, byte tier), which WEB renders “Of the increase of his government”; the gloss actually paired with it is “The zeal of Yahweh of Armies will perform this.” (web:Isa.9.7 = oshb:Isa.9.6), which renders a different clause of the same verse, "קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה זֹּֽאת" (oshb:Isa.9.6 = web:Isa.9.7, byte tier). Two further mismatches: the six-token opening splice "כִּ֣י לֹ֣א מוּעָף֮ לַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מוּצָ֣ק לָהּ֒" (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1, byte tier) is glossed with the whole of web:Isa.9.1 through “Galilee of the nations.”; and the throne-name splice (oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6, byte tier) is glossed “His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.” (web:Isa.9.6 = oshb:Isa.9.5), which also renders "וַיִּקְרָ֨א שְׁמ֜וֹ" (oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6, byte tier), outside the splice. The doubled-token engagement itself is correct - both staged forms are quoted and the medial final mem is correctly called letter bytes plus ketiv/qere apparatus, not a special-letter seg.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: pair the doubled-token splice with WEB's own rendering of it, and re-cut the other two glosses to their splice extents. No span change.

findings.claim: Four in-zone structured refs stand bare in the row's prose, one of them with no dual anywhere in its field.
findings.grounds: Under the ratified two-zone rule every structured ref touching WEB ch 9 or MT 8:23 / MT ch 9 carries an explicit dual or numeric qualifier. In the boundary_rationale, "web:Isa.9.8's fresh declarative sentence" carries no dual at any point in the field; and the first mentions of "(oshb:Isa.8.23, byte tier)", "(oshb:Isa.9.5, byte tier)" and "(oshb:Isa.9.6, byte tier)" are bare, the dual arriving only in a later clause of the same sentence. boundary_evidence_refs is fully dual-cited and every pairing there is arithmetically right (MT 8:23 = WEB 9:1; MT 9:1 = WEB 9:2; MT 9:2 = WEB 9:3; MT 9:5 = WEB 9:6; MT 9:6 = WEB 9:7; MT 9:7 = WEB 9:8), and both in-span ketiv/qere verses (MT 9:2, MT 9:6) and the MT 9:5 exegesis note are disclosed at single-witness.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: add the dual at each bare in-zone ref, e.g. web:Isa.9.8 = oshb:Isa.9.7. No span change.
